## CPython 3.13 Free Threading and Extension Imports

CPython 3.13 introduced experimental free threading as a configuration in which the Global Interpreter Lock (GIL) can be disabled. What happens next depends in part on the extensions an application imports.

If an extension lacks an explicit declaration that it supports this mode, importing it produces a warning and enables the GIL. The declaration mechanism differs depending on whether the extension uses multi-phase or single-phase initialization.

Declaring support for free threading is a compatibility signal, not a guarantee that an extension is thread-safe. Extension authors have a separate responsibility to make the extension’s code thread-safe.
